subject: red-eyed tree frog
title: These Frog Eggs Feel a Snake Biting and Hatch in Seconds to Escape

scenes.text: These frog eggs know when a snake is eating them.
Red-eyed tree frogs stick their eggs on leaves above ponds. They normally hatch after a week.
But when a snake bites the clutch, the embryos feel the shaking and bail out.
Each squirts an enzyme from its snout, melts a hole in the egg and wriggles free in as little as six seconds.
They rain into the pond as tadpoles, days early.
Raindrops shake the eggs too. They stay put. They only jump for the snake.

description:
Red-eyed tree frog embryos can tell a snake attack from a rainstorm, and hatch in seconds to get away.
The eggs hang on leaves over ponds in rain forests from Mexico to Colombia and normally hatch after six or seven days. Karen Warkentin's lab at Boston University found that when a snake bites into a clutch, older embryos release an egg-dissolving enzyme from glands on the snout and thrash out, in 6 to 50 seconds, then drop into the water below. Raindrop vibrations do not set them off. Escaping early has a cost: the premature tadpoles are smaller and easier for pond predators to catch.
Would you jump early or wait it out? Comment below.
